APUSH AUDIO · UNIT 1

The Collision:
Europe Sails West

Episode 2 — Maya asks, Marcus answers.

beats.chain_caption: Three motives in three words: gold, God, glory — the short answer and the fine print.

beats.html:
RIVALRY
An arms race
with sails.
No crown wants to watch its rival sail off to Asia alone — so they ask the pope to draw a line.

THE MIDDLEMAN
1453: Constantinople falls,
tariffs go up.
The Ottomans charge whatever they want for the land routes — suddenly your own route to Asia looks worth the risk.

PORTUGAL'S EDGE
The guy who
never sailed anywhere.
Prince Henry the Navigator never went on a single voyage — he bankrolled the captains who did.

beats.chain_caption: Light fast ships, latitude from the stars, a course you can hold — the first tech stack that could cross an ocean on purpose.

beats.html:
MAYA'S TAKE
A compass and a prayer
is a hard no.
Crossing an ocean on 15th-century tech — queasy on the ferry to Catalina, harder no on the Atlantic.

SPAIN, 1492
Just kicked the Moors
out of Granada.
Same year, the crown suddenly has money and attention — for a Genoese sailor with a wild pitch.

COLUMBUS
Wrong about
basically everything.
Not the shape of the earth — the size. Asia was ten thousand miles west, not a few thousand. Lands October 12, 1492, in the Bahamas.

FOUR VOYAGES
Zero North America.
Four voyages, never set foot on the continent — but Spain's holding new islands, and Portugal is furious.

THE POPE STEPS IN
He just divides up
the planet?
Pretty much. Two Catholic crowns, one pope, and a line through an ocean they had barely seen.

beats.chain_caption: 370 leagues west of Cape Verde — Spain west, Portugal east — and everyone else ignored it completely.

beats.html:
ONE DOWN
In 1972 it got
a name.
Alfred Crosby called it the Columbian Exchange: plants, animals, people, and diseases crossing the Atlantic in both directions.

THE EXCHANGE
Potatoes east,
horses west.
Maize, potatoes, tomatoes sail east and feed a population boom. Wheat, sugarcane, rice sail west — a lot of groceries crossing an ocean.

WESTBOUND
The horse remakes
the Plains.
Horses, cattle, pigs sail west — and yes, Idaho potatoes are American. Maya's whole personality, reconsidered.

beats.chain_caption: Disease crossed one way — smallpox, measles, influenza — and cleared the ground before the conquest even started.

beats.html:
THE DEBATED ONE
Anything go back east,
disease-wise?
Syphilis — maybe. Nobody's fully sure. Two down.

THE CONQUEST PATTERN
A few hundred?
Against an empire?
The Aztec capital falls by 1521. Guns and horses help — and smallpox helps more.

THE PART PEOPLE SKIP
Tens of thousands
of Native allies.
Peoples the Aztecs had spent years bullying marched with the Spaniards — same story in Peru with the Inca a decade later.

THE ENCOMIENDA
A grant: labor and tribute —
supposed to.
A colonist gets the Native people of an area; in return he's supposed to protect them and convert them. Supposed to.

ONE FRIAR BREAKS RANKS
Bartolomé
de las Casas.
Gives up his own grant, lobbies the crown for decades — and in 1542 the crown passes the New Laws. No more enslaving Natives.

DID IT WORK?
Barely.
The colonists nearly revolted; the crown watered the laws down. But the question got on the record: subjects to convert, or labor to use? And that's all three.

RECAP · 1 OF 3
Tordesillas.
1494. Line in the Atlantic, 370 leagues west of Cape Verde. West to Spain, east to Portugal — which is why Brazil speaks Portuguese.

RECAP · 2 OF 3
The Exchange.
Stuff goes both ways — except the bad stuff mostly goes one way. Disease sailed west; crops went both directions.

RECAP · 3 OF 3
Encomienda.
Grant of Native labor and tribute, supposedly for Christianity. Brutal in practice — Las Casas blows the whistle, 1542, barely enforced.

QUESTION 1 OF 2
Name one thing Europe got from the Columbian Exchange — and one thing the Americas got.

Europe: potatoes, maize, or tomatoes. Americas: horses, wheat, or sugarcane. One each.

QUESTION 2 OF 2
What was the encomienda, in one sentence?

A Spanish grant giving a colonist the labor and tribute of Native people — supposedly in exchange for converting them. Brutal in practice.

CHECK YOUR BOXES
Episode two
in the books.
Next time: Spain plants its flag — and England starts watching.

EPISODE 2
Two worlds, one ocean —
No going back.
